# Text Classification with Natural Language Processing: Comprehensive Learning Guide

## Course Overview

This advanced course teaches you how to build, train, and optimize machine learning systems that automatically categorize text into predefined labels. Text classification is one of the most practical NLP applications, powering spam detection, sentiment analysis, topic modeling, intent recognition, and content moderation across industry.

**Who this is for:**
- Software engineers preparing for ML/NLP-focused roles at tech companies
- Backend engineers transitioning into machine learning
- Data scientists building production NLP systems
- Candidates interviewing at companies like Google, Meta, Amazon, Microsoft, and OpenAI

**Why it matters for interview prep:**
Text classification appears in ~30% of NLP technical interviews and is the foundation for understanding more complex tasks (named entity recognition, semantic similarity, question answering). Mastery demonstrates practical understanding of the ML pipeline: data preprocessing, feature engineering, model selection, evaluation, and deployment considerations. Interviewers value candidates who can explain trade-offs between bag-of-words, TF-IDF, embeddings, and transformer-based approaches.

---

## Core Topics Covered

- **Text Preprocessing & Normalization**: Tokenization, lowercasing, stemming, lemmatization, stopword removal, handling special characters
- **Feature Extraction Methods**: Bag-of-Words (BoW), TF-IDF, Word2Vec embeddings, FastText, GloVe, and contextual embeddings (BERT, RoBERTa)
- **Classic ML Classifiers**: Naive Bayes, Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machines, Random Forests for text classification
- **Neural Network Approaches**: Feedforward networks, CNNs for text, RNNs/LSTMs/GRUs with attention mechanisms
- **Transformer-Based Models**: Fine-tuning BERT, DistilBERT, and other pre-trained language models for classification
- **Evaluation Metrics & Validation**: Precision, recall, F1-score, ROC-AUC, confusion matrix, cross-validation, class imbalance handling
- **Advanced Techniques**: Data augmentation, ensemble methods, active learning, transfer learning, multi-label classification
- **Production Considerations**: Model optimization, inference speed, memory constraints, versioning, monitoring drift

---

## Learning Path Workflow

### **Phase 1: Foundations (Weeks 1–2) — 20 Practice Tasks**
Start with the fundamentals of text processing and classical methods.

1. **Text Preprocessing Basics** (5 tasks)
   - Implement tokenization from scratch
   - Build a stemmer/lemmatizer using NLTK
   - Remove stopwords and handle punctuation
   - Normalize text (lowercasing, whitespace)
   - Clean real-world messy data (URLs, HTML tags, emojis)

2. **Bag-of-Words & TF-IDF** (7 tasks)
   - Implement BoW vectorizer manually
   - Build TF-IDF from scratch
   - Compare BoW vs. TF-IDF on a dataset
   - Handle sparse matrices efficiently
   - Analyze top features per class
   - Implement L1/L2 normalization
   - Understand vocabulary size impact

3. **Classic ML Classifiers** (8 tasks)
   - Naive Bayes on binary classification
   - Logistic regression for text (from scratch)
   - SVM with linear and RBF kernels
   - Train Random Forest on text features
   - Compare classifiers on same dataset
   - Hyperparameter tuning for each
   - Handle class imbalance with class weights
   - Interpret model coefficients/feature importance

### **Phase 2: Embeddings & Deep Learning (Weeks 3–5) — 35 Practice Tasks**

4. **Word Embeddings** (8 tasks)
   - Train Word2Vec (Skip-gram and CBOW)
   - Use pre-trained FastText embeddings
   - Load and use GloVe vectors
   - Implement average pooling (document-level embeddings)
   - Explore embedding space (nearest neighbors, analogies)
   - Compare embedding quality across methods
   - Handle out-of-vocabulary words
   - Visualize embeddings with t-SNE/UMAP

5. **Feedforward Neural Networks** (8 tasks)
   - Build simple dense network classifier
   - Implement embedding layer + dropout
   - Experiment with different architectures
   - Add regularization (L1, L2, dropout)
   - Implement custom training loop (PyTorch/TensorFlow)
   - Optimize learning rate with schedulers
   - Handle variable-length sequences
   - Implement early stopping

6. **Convolutional & Recurrent Networks** (10 tasks)
   - Implement 1D CNN for text classification
   - Stack multiple filter sizes
   - Build LSTM/GRU sequence classifiers
   - Use bidirectional architectures
   - Implement attention mechanism manually
   - Combine CNN + attention
   - Compare RNN architectures (LSTM vs. GRU)
   - Handle padded sequences in batches
   - Implement hierarchical attention (words → sentences)
   - Use pre-trained embeddings with neural models

7. **Sequence Processing & Batching** (9 tasks)
   - Implement padding and masking
   - Create DataLoaders for NLP tasks
   - Handle variable-length sequences in batches
   - Implement bucketing for efficiency
   - Pack padded sequences (PyTorch)
   - Create custom collate functions
   - Debug tensor shape mismatches
   - Implement stratified sampling
   - Work with imbalanced datasets

### **Phase 3: Transformer Models & Transfer Learning (Weeks 6–8) — 35 Practice Tasks**

8. **BERT & Fine-Tuning** (12 tasks)
   - Load pre-trained BERT from HuggingFace
   - Tokenize text for BERT (special tokens, segment IDs)
   - Fine-tune BERT on custom dataset
   - Compare BERT vs. DistilBERT vs. RoBERTa
   - Implement classification head on top of [CLS] token
   - Handle long documents (truncation vs. sliding window)
   - Freeze/unfreeze encoder layers
   - Implement discriminative learning rates
   - Use mixed precision training
   - Compare fine-tuning vs. feature extraction
   - Implement custom loss functions
   - Validate on held-out test set

9. **Advanced Transfer Learning** (10 tasks)
   - Multi-task learning for text classification
   - Domain adaptation techniques
   - Few-shot learning with pre-trained models
   - Data augmentation (back-translation, EDA, mixup)
   - Prompt-based few-shot classification (GPT-style)
   - Meta-learning approaches
   - Continual learning / catastrophic forgetting
   - Knowledge distillation from large to small models
   - Test-time augmentation
   - Uncertainty estimation

10. **Multi-Label & Multi-Task** (8 tasks)
    - Implement multi-label classification
    - Use sigmoid activation + BCELoss
    - Handle label imbalance in multi-label scenarios
    - Implement multi-task learning (shared + task-specific heads)
    - Threshold optimization for multilabel
    - Evaluate multi-label metrics (hamming loss, subset accuracy)
    - Hierarchical label structures
    - Joint classification + auxiliary tasks

11. **Production & Optimization** (5 tasks)
    - Quantize BERT models
    - Implement model compression (pruning, distillation)
    - Optimize inference latency
    - Batch inference for throughput
    - Deploy using ONNX or TorchScript
    - Implement caching strategies
    - Monitor inference latency & memory

### **Phase 4: Evaluation, Debugging & Interview Practice (Weeks 9–10) — 20 Practice Tasks**

12. **Evaluation & Metrics** (8 tasks)
    - Implement precision, recall, F1 from scratch
    - Compute confusion matrix and interpret
    - ROC-AUC curves and thresholding
    - Per-class performance analysis
    - Cross-validation strategies (k-fold, stratified)
    - Handle class imbalance metrics
    - Implement custom metrics
    - Statistical significance testing

13. **Error Analysis & Debugging** (7 tasks)
    - Implement error analysis pipeline
    - Identify classes with poor performance
    - Analyze misclassified examples
    - Detect and handle label noise
    - Dataset shift detection
    - Visualize decision boundaries
    - Debug overfitting vs. underfitting
    - Implement ablation studies
